Sirius A is a hotter, younger star, and it pushes back. Every tier unlocks in order, in the same three steps:
1. §9milestones§r on the current star;
2. §9the core§r, right-clicked into escrow;
3. §9the transition§r, a live event you have to survive.

§5§lMILESTONES§r On Sol: §920,000,000 L Raw Stellar Plasma§r made and §92 h Resonant§r (real time). The GUI and scanner count them, and they stay with the controller through a wrench.

§5§lCORE§r Right-click the controller with the §9Stellar Mass Core§r (Condensate Assembling, 256,000 L Entangled Raw Star Matter). It is consumed §lonly§r when the transition succeeds. Sneak-punch with an empty hand to take it back.

§5§lMASS INFUSION§r Build the §9beam band§r (hologram stack 2: 2,856 Beam Band Casing) and bring compression to tier 2. Buffer §95,000,000 L Raw Stellar Plasma§r plus Sirius A's first cycle, then put §9Star Chart: Sirius A§r in the slot while Sol burns. For 10 minutes the plasma pours into Sol and P is pushed §9+4 a second§r, so your rig must hold. Survive it and Sol becomes Sirius A, with T2 unlocked for good. Fail and you lose Sol and the plasma, never the core.

§5§lRUN§r Each cycle: §912,500,000 L Hydrogen + 12,500,000 L Helium + 25,000 L Raw Stellar Plasma§r and 6.04 × 10¹¹ EU (about 1 A UXV), for §92,500 L Excited Stellar Plasma Mixture§r. A relight takes a charge and a 200,000,000 L seed of each gas.

§5§lTRIMS§r As Sol (Helium P −2, Hydrogen P +2 per 1,000 L), now up to 20 units a second. The beam band's 6 stellar sockets take input hatches for the star's fluids.

[warn]Sirius A drifts P +2 a second and breaches if left alone: run the rig. Helium leaves §lash§r, −0.5 % yield per 1,000 L dosed that second, so a two-stage rig (small doses near 0, big ones far out) beats full-blast valves.[/warn]

[note]A higher Eye still hosts lower stars, at ×2 parallel per tier above. There is one live star per Eye.[/note]

§2§lDONE WHEN§r you have held the core and the chart before the core goes into escrow (that task latches), and then 1,000 L of Excited Stellar Plasma Mixture, Sirius A's first product.
